step.title: Welcome
step.prompt: Hello Seamus, it is lovely to spend this time with you today. Let us settle in and enjoy some memories together.
step.caregiverTip: Start with a warm, calm tone to help Seamus feel comfortable and oriented.

step.title: Showband Music
step.prompt: Seamus, I have a showband record from the 1950s here. Let us listen to this together.
followUps: Do you remember the dance halls in Cork?
step.caregiverTip: Showband music was the heartbeat of 1950s Cork; he may enjoy tapping his feet or humming along.

step.title: The Searchers

entity.name: The Searchers
entity.description: The Searchers (1956), directed by John Ford and starring John Wayne, Jeffrey Hunter and Vera Miles, is an epic Western-adventure that follows a Civil War veteran who spends years searching the Plains for his kidnapped niece. Framed against Monument Valley vistas, the film blends action and long-range pursuit with a psychological focus on obsession, vengeance and racial tension. Its narrative probes identity and belonging on the frontier while maintaining a brooding, morally ambiguous tone.

step.prompt: Here is a still from The Searchers, the 1956 Western. What do you think of this scene?
followUps: Do you enjoy these classic Westerns?
step.caregiverTip: The Searchers was a popular film in the 1950s; he may appreciate the familiar landscape and the classic storytelling.
step.mediaHint: Search 'The Searchers 1956 film still' on Google Images

step.title: Glen Rovers
step.prompt: I was thinking about the hurling matches at the Glen Rovers club. Tell me about the games you used to watch in the 1960s.
followUps: Who were the best players you saw?
step.caregiverTip: Glen Rovers is a deep passion; focus on the excitement of the matches he attended in 1960s Cork.

step.title: Rhythmic Clapping
step.prompt: Let us clap along to a lively tune from the 1950s, Seamus. Shall we keep the beat together?
step.caregiverTip: Use a simple, steady rhythm from a 1950s dance tune to encourage gentle movement.
step.mediaHint: Search '1950s Irish dance music' on YouTube

step.title: Closing
step.prompt: Thank you for sharing these moments with me today, Seamus. It has been a pleasure.
step.caregiverTip: End with a gentle touch or a warm smile to conclude the session.
